caption:
OpenAI has raised $11 billion so far in a new round that values it at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reported.
In September it was reportedly aiming for up to $30 billion. Now the round may top out around $20 billion.
Investors are pulling back on Anthropic's IPO price too.

Is the AI money boom starting to cool?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch, Reuters · Photo: rappler.com

paragraphs.text: OpenAI has secured $11 billion in a new funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, November 6, 2026, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters, which carried the Bloomberg report, described the $11 billion as the initial part of a larger round.

The round has not closed. According to TechCrunch's summary of the Bloomberg report, it is expected to close in the coming weeks, and one person told Bloomberg that the final total could be about $20 billion. TechCrunch said it had contacted OpenAI for comment.

The figures fall short of what OpenAI was reported to be seeking only weeks ago. In late September, Bloomberg reported that the company was aiming to raise up to $30 billion at a valuation of $1.4 trillion. Two investors told Reuters on Friday that both the target amount and the target valuation had come down.

SoftBank and MGX are participating in the round, according to the investors who spoke to Reuters, as reported by The American Bazaar. The reports did not name other investors or say how much each one is putting in.
A cooler market for AI giants

OpenAI is not the only large AI developer facing more cautious buyers. Bloomberg reported on the same day that potential buyers of shares in Anthropic's planned initial public offering were considering a valuation well below what the company had targeted. TechCrunch said some think it could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with about $2 trillion that investors were reportedly expecting a month earlier. Reuters put the potential figure at about $1.5 trillion.

Both TechCrunch and The American Bazaar linked the cooling sentiment to the Democratic Party's strong showing in the U.S. midterm elections and to negative voter sentiment toward data center construction, with many investors expecting more regulatory hurdles for the industry.

The new money also arrives as OpenAI's own listing slips. The company had previously indicated it would go public in 2026 but delayed those plans, and it is now expected to hold its initial public offering in 2027, according to a Reuters report cited by TechCrunch.

An $11 billion raise at $1.25 trillion is still an enormous sum by any normal standard. The shift is in leverage. A few months ago, investors were competing for access to the leading AI labs. The reported cuts to both OpenAI's target and Anthropic's expected IPO price suggest that buyers now feel able to push back on terms, which matters for companies that need very large sums for chips and data centers.

The next marker is the final size of the round when it closes, expected in the coming weeks. A total near $20 billion would confirm the lower target, and the price set for Anthropic's IPO will show whether the same pullback applies across the sector.
